# Results -- Study 255 (Fear-Greed) on real ^GSPC weekly tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: each Friday
read the curated CNN Fear & Greed Index; go **long** ^GSPC in Extreme Fear
(F&G < 25), **short** in Extreme Greed (F&G >= 75), flat otherwise; hold one
week (one-week execution lag, trade next Monday's open). Pinned against the
unconditional weekly drift, a shuffled-sentiment null, and a synthetic positive
control. **Price-only**: ^GSPC carries no dividends, so the long-only fear
excess is understated by the dividend yield; the fear-minus-greed spread is
dividend-neutral. As-of **2026-06-12**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint (last row) |
|--------|--------|-------|----------------------|
| Curated CNN Fear & Greed (monthly anchors -> weekly) x ^GSPC weekly close (repo cache, split-only/price-only) | 2011-09-30 -> 2026-06-12 | 768 weeks (767 with forward return) | `6d62af784bd5` |

The Fear & Greed series is a hardcoded month-end anchor table (digitised from
CNN's published history) interpolated to weekly Fridays. It is a regime-faithful
proxy, not a tick-exact reconstruction -- the contrarian signal acts only on the
fear/greed *regime*, which the anchors capture.

## Forward weekly return by Fear & Greed band

| Band | n weeks | Forward return (ann) | HAC *t* | Hit rate |
|------|---------|----------------------|---------|----------|
| Extreme Fear (<25) | 65 | +14.20%/yr | +0.61 | 0.523 |
| Fear (25-44) | 183 | +6.68%/yr | +0.73 | 0.541 |
| Neutral (45-55) | 165 | +15.24%/yr | +2.26 | 0.618 |
| Greed (56-74) | 332 | +17.23%/yr | **+5.33** | 0.617 |
| Extreme Greed (>=75) | 22 | +18.17%/yr | +1.40 | 0.591 |

Unconditional forward weekly return: **+14.05%/yr**. The pattern is the
**opposite** of the contrarian claim: forward returns broadly *rise* with the
sentiment band, and the only band with a strong t-stat is **Greed** (+5.33) --
because greed weeks coincide with the bull-market trend, not because greed
predicts more upside. Extreme Fear weeks (+14.2%/yr, t = 0.61) do not beat the
unconditional drift in any meaningful way.

## Primary specification -- the contrarian fear-minus-greed spread

| Series | Mean | Ann. | HAC *t* | Ann. Sharpe | Hit |
|--------|------|------|---------|-------------|-----|
| **Spread (long fear, short greed)** | **+1.31 bps/wk** | **+0.68%/yr** | **+0.41** | +0.07 | 0.056 |
| Long-only fear excess over market | +0.29 bps/wk | +0.15%/yr | +0.01 | -- | -- |
| Linear sentiment tilt (slope per 50 F&G pts) | +16.8 bps | -- | +0.53 | -- | -- |

- The contrarian spread HAC *t* = **+0.41** -- nowhere near the *t* >= 2 bar.
- Block-bootstrap 95% CI on the spread Sharpe (ann): **[-0.24, +0.45]**, with
  **33% of resamples negative** -- the interval straddles zero.
- The linear sentiment slope is +16.8 bps per 50 F&G points (*t* = 0.53) and is
  the **wrong sign** for the contrarian claim (it implies higher sentiment ->
  higher next-week return) and is statistically indistinguishable from zero.

## Sub-period analysis -- no era rescues it

| Period | Spread/yr | HAC *t* | n weeks |
|--------|-----------|---------|---------|
| 2011-2016 | +2.71%/yr | +1.32 | 275 |
| 2017-2021 | +0.66%/yr | +0.15 | 261 |
| 2022-2026 | -1.70%/yr | -0.64 | 231 |

No sub-period clears *t* = 2; the most recent era is negative. There is no
stable contrarian edge in any slice.

## Shuffled-sentiment null -- the signal is indistinguishable from noise

Permuting the Fear & Greed column 2,000 times (breaking any link to forward
returns) gives a null spread-mean distribution centred at **+1.40 bps/wk**
(std 2.64 bps). The *real* spread mean is **+1.31 bps/wk** -- it sits at the
**47.5th percentile** of the shuffled null. Real sentiment carries no more
timing information than a random relabelling.

## Tradability -- turnover and costs

The overlay is flat **88.7%** of weeks (Extreme Fear/Greed are rare): ~8.5%
long, ~2.9% short, with **~2.8 round-trips per year** (41 trades over 767 weeks).

| One-way cost / borrow | Net spread | Net HAC *t* |
|-----------------------|-----------|-------------|
| 5 bps one-way + 50 bps/yr borrow | +0.53%/yr | +0.31 |

Costs are tiny (the strategy barely trades), so the verdict is not a
cost-driven death -- there is simply **no gross signal to erode**. Even gross,
*t* = 0.41.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds the effect when it is planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`), the same overlay
recovers a planted contrarian premium monotonically:

| Planted premium | Spread mean/wk | Spread HAC *t* |
|-----------------|----------------|----------------|
| 0 bps (null) | -5.66 bps (chance) | -1.96 (within null band) |
| +60 bps | +3.76 bps | +1.32 |
| +120 bps | +13.18 bps | **+3.85** |

The engine clears *t* > 2 when a real contrarian effect exists -- it just
finds nothing on the real Fear & Greed tape.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Contrarian spread HAC *t* = +0.41; bootstrap Sharpe CI
  [-0.24, +0.45] straddles zero (33% negative); the real spread sits at the
  47.5th percentile of a shuffled-sentiment null; the band pattern is the
  *opposite* of the claim (returns rise with greed, an artefact of the bull
  trend). Literature (Brown-Cliff 2004, Welch-Goyal 2008) agrees that aggregate
  sentiment has little near-term predictive power. **NONE.**
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** There is no gross edge to trade; the overlay is
  flat 89% of the time and even gross-of-cost the spread is *t* = 0.41. The
  apparent "Extreme Fear is a buy" folk wisdom is a story told about a
  ~14%/yr unconditional bull market, not a timing signal. **MIRAGE.**
- **Survivorship -- n/a** (single index, no cross-section). The honest caveat
  on the Signal axis is instead the **curated-proxy** nature of the hardcoded
  Fear & Greed series and the **price-only** ^GSPC tape.
